Pregabalin produced a significantly greater reduction in IRLSSG severity scores at both week 6 (median change -5.0 vs 0.0 points, p<0.001) and week 12 (median change -9.0 vs -2.0 points, p<0.001), and 64% of pregabalin-treated patients achieved categorical improvement versus 28% with placebo (adjusted OR 4.9, 95% CI 1.8–13.4, p=0.002). Pregabalin was well tolerated with only mild, transient sedation as the primary adverse effect and no serious adverse events.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1) IQR values for RLS scores are reported as single IQR values (range width) rather than lower/upper bounds — e.g., pregabalin baseline IQR: 10.5, placebo baseline IQR: 11.0; these cannot be split into iqr_low/iqr_high without additional information, so iqr_low/iqr_high are set to null. 2) Change-score IQRs are also given as single values (pregabalin week 6: IQR 6.5; placebo week 6: IQR 3.0; pregabalin week 12: IQR 9.5; placebo week 12: IQR 4.0) — similarly left as null. 3) The pregabalin dose is never specified in the paper. 4) Per-arm randomization numbers are not reported; only the total enrolled (103) and total completers (72, split 36/36) are given. 5) Dropout allocation between arms (31 total dropouts) is not specified per arm. 6) The baseline calcium IQR for pregabalin is 0.95 and for placebo is 1.3; marginal baseline difference noted (p=0.04) but both within normal range. 7) The logistic regression log-odds is reported as 1.7 ± 0.5 — the ± here represents the standard error of the coefficient. 8) Some quantitative EEG/animal model data (LH ratios, clustering distances) are extracted narratively only; full per-animal data are in figures and the public dataset. 9) The between-group comparison for change scores at week 6 and week 12 is reported as p<0.001 (not exact). 10) A marginal baseline calcium difference existed between groups (pregabalin: 9.5 mg/dL IQR 0.95 vs placebo: 9.0 mg/dL IQR 1.3, p=0.04). 11) Outcome 3 (linear regression slope) is a secondary analytic result; R² values: pregabalin 0.25, placebo 0.01; p-values: pregabalin p<0.001, placebo p=0.20.

summary: This quasi-experimental parallel-group study conducted at a single hemodialysis unit in Jakarta, Indonesia enrolled 80 chronic kidney disease patients on hemodialysis with restless legs syndrome (RLS), randomized to intradialytic aerobic plus stretching exercise (n=40) or a warm-up control (n=40) over 4 weeks (8 sessions). The intervention group showed a statistically significant reduction in IRLSSG categorical RLS score from 2.12 to 1.56 (change -0.56, p=0.001), while the control group showed no significant change (2.09 to 2.19, p=0.164). The authors concluded that intradialytic aerobic and stretching exercise with audio-visual media effectively reduces RLS severity in hemodialysis patients.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The IRLSSG scores reported (means ~2.06–2.19) appear to be categorical severity codes (0=mild, 1=moderate, 2=severe) rather than raw 0–40 scale totals; this is an unusual reporting format — the paper describes a 3-level categorical outcome but uses means. SDs are not reported for any outcome measure. The abstract states pre-test control mean as 2.06 while Table 2 states 2.09 — the Table 2 value (2.09) was used as it is from the primary results table. The abstract also mentions pre-test intervention mean of 2.12 consistent with Table 2. The paper states 40 per group but also mentions subgroup n=20 per group in a methods paragraph — 40 per group is used based on the abstract and results section which clearly states N=80 total with 40 per group. No SDs reported for outcome data. Between-group p-value not explicitly reported; only within-group paired t-test p-values given (p=0.001 for intervention, p=0.164 for control). Demographic table shows intervention arm n=20 female (60%) and n=16 male (40%), but the text says majority male 42 (52.5%) — there is an inconsistency in the table where intervention arm shows 16 male (40%) and 24 female (60%) which contradicts this. The table column headers appear to show n=20 per group but the main text says n=40 per group — this is a likely table formatting error in the original publication. All demographic percentages extracted from table as-is.

summary: This single-arm retrospective pre-post study examined the effects of Korean medical treatment (herbal medicine, acupuncture, and oriental psychotherapy) in 13 RLS patients treated for 4 weeks and a subset of 6 patients treated for 8 weeks at a single neuropsychiatric clinic in Seoul. At 4 weeks, state anxiety, trait anxiety, depression (BDI-2), somatic anxiety (BAI), and state anger improved significantly, while RLS severity (IRLS) decreased but did not reach significance (p=0.062). At 8 weeks, RLS severity became significantly improved (mean change -8.17 points, p=0.019), as did all anxiety and depression measures, suggesting that longer treatment duration may be needed for RLS-specific symptom improvement.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is NOT an RCT — it is a single-arm quasi-experimental pre-post study with no control group, no randomization, and no blinding. The paper is written in Korean with an English abstract; the full text is in Korean but data tables are bilingual. Two overlapping analysis cohorts are reported: n=13 (4-week completers) and n=6 (8-week completers, a subset of the 13). Baseline values for the 4-week (n=13) and 8-week (n=6) cohorts differ slightly because different patients completed 8 weeks; both sets of baseline values are extracted separately in arm_results. Between_group_effects fields are used to encode pre-post within-arm paired t-test results (one-tailed), not true between-group comparisons. The paper did not report IRB approval at the time of study conduct (noted as a limitation). No adverse events were reported. The 8-week BDI-2 baseline in the text reads 21.33±14.46 which matches Table 3 value; no discrepancy. Trait anger (STAXI-T) slightly increased at 8 weeks (20.00 to 20.33), which is correctly reflected.

risk_of_bias.key_concern: This is a non-randomized single-arm open-label study with no concurrent control group; the comparison with historic ropinirole trials is an indirect meta-analysis and the extreme placebo effect known in RLS trials (40-75%) cannot be disentangled from device effect.

summary: This single-arm open-label 8-week trial (n=30) evaluated a foot-wrap device (restiffic) applying targeted pressure to the abductor hallucis and flexor hallucis brevis muscles in adults with moderate-to-severe primary RLS. The primary outcome — mean IRLSSG Rating Scale score — decreased significantly from 25.05 (SD 5.33) at baseline to 7.83 (SD 6.33) at day 56, a mean change of 17.22 points (P<0.001), and nightly sleep loss decreased from ~120 to ~22 minutes. In an indirect comparison via meta-analysis against three historic ropinirole RCTs, the device change score (17.22) exceeded ropinirole (12.0, SD 0.86) and placebo (8.9, SD 0.86), and the CGI responder rate (90%) was significantly higher than ropinirole (63%, P<0.05); however, the absence of randomization and a concurrent control group means placebo effects cannot be excluded.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. This is NOT a randomized controlled trial — it is a single-arm open-label repeated-measures study (ABCD design: baseline without device, treatment, washout, treatment). The study_design fields for randomization and allocation concealment are null accordingly. 2. The 'arms' in outcomes 9 and 10 (arm_id=2 for ropinirole, arm_id=3 for placebo) are historic meta-analysis comparators extracted from eTable 2 — they are NOT concurrent trial arms. 3. The 'between_group_effects' for the device vs. ropinirole and placebo represent indirect cross-trial comparisons, not within-trial randomized contrasts. Effect values calculated as device change (17.22) minus ropinirole change (12.0) = 5.22 and device change minus placebo change (8.9) = 8.32. 4. The placebo CI in eTable 2 appears to have a typo: '8.9-.86' is likely '8.74-9.06' (i.e. mean ± 0.08*1.96) — extracted as stated. 5. Table 2 contains mean (SD) for all 10 IRLSSG items at baseline, final, and follow-up — only summary IRLSSG item scores were extracted in outcomes 4 and 11 rather than all 10 items separately to manage output size; all 10 item scores are present in Table 2. 6. Table 1 contains per-patient period means and SDs across 30 patients — individual patient data not re-extracted into arm_results. 7. Figure 3 shows IRLSSG scores by survey day — numerical values not extractable from figure description alone. 8. The eTable 2 also contains individual study data for Bogan et al (N=380), Trenkwalder et al (N=284), and Walters et al (N=266) — extracted as meta-analysis weighted means only; individual study breakdown available in eTable 2. 9. Follow-up survey conducted at mean 15.6 (SD 6) months (range 8.4-28.8 months) in 17/30 patients (57%). 10. n_randomized is null because this is not a randomized trial; 47 enrolled, 36 received intervention, 30 included in final analysis per modified ITT with LOCF.
